vision.statement: Warpgogol Platform uses Compass as the repository-wide operating model for AI-assisted engineering. The goal is deterministic, architecture-aware work across a Turborepo that contains reusable kernel packages in `packages/` and deployable sites in `apps/`.

operating-principles.principle: Read and update machine-readable repository contracts before changing architecture, shared behavior, or high-risk boundaries.
Treat generated code as a compilation target of approved semantic intent, not as free-form improvisation.
Prefer XML documents for large AI-facing architecture context, plans, reports, and logs.
Keep repository rules, Compass documents, and implementation synchronized so that future agents inherit truthful context.

use-case.action: Triggers the changelog pipeline on a weekly or monthly schedule, or manually via CLI.
use-case.goal: Produce a versioned changelog file and bump SemVer without manual intervention.

use-case.action: Collects git commits for the release window, extracts tree hash, diff summary, and sanitizes all text fields before AI processing.
use-case.goal: Feed safe, token-efficient, prompt-injection-free input to AI agents.

use-case.action: Classifies each commit (type, severity, module, isBreaking, confidence) using deterministic rules first and LLM as fallback. Results are cached in SQLite WAL with a composite key.
use-case.goal: Stable, idempotent classification resilient to cherry-pick and squash merge.

use-case.action: Clusters 50+ technical commits into 5-7 business-level groups based on file path overlap and semantic proximity.
use-case.goal: Produce a human-readable changelog grouped by feature, not by raw commit.

use-case.action: Generates each changelog section as coherent prose in a single prompt per group. Past tense, no marketing language.
use-case.goal: Deliver a changelog readable by users, not a raw commit log.

use-case.action: Calculates next SemVer deterministically. Breaking changes with AI confidence below 0.85 produce a warning and manual review flag instead of an automatic bump. Major version is hard-locked.
use-case.goal: Prevent accidental major bumps; flag uncertain breaking changes for human review.

use-case.action: Writes versioned changelog files (changelog-YYYY-MM-DD-vX.Y.Z.md) atomically via tmp+rename. Rebuilds CHANGELOG.md index entirely. Restores dynamic markers if missing.
use-case.goal: Guarantee atomic, idempotent, collision-free file output.

use-case.action: Runs the changelog pipeline on schedule, caches the SQLite DB between runs, and commits results automatically.
use-case.goal: Zero-touch changelog generation in CI without token waste or API rate limit errors.

use-case.action: Onboards a new site to the shared Lagebild CRM sync worker via `lagebild.tenant.add`, then sets per-tenant secrets via `wrangler secret put`.
use-case.goal: Add a new client to the multi-tenant CRM buffer without creating a per-site Worker folder (RFC-0186).

use-case.action: Reads enabled tenants from Supabase `sync_tenants`, resolves secret references from Worker env, and processes each tenant's `sync_outbox` rows with isolation.
use-case.goal: Keep every tenant's CRM data in sync without one tenant's failure affecting others (RFC-0186).

use-case.action: Reads the root Compass documents before planning or editing a cross-workspace task.
use-case.goal: Preserve architectural intent and avoid shallow local-only changes.

use-case.action: Updates shared packages in `packages/` and validates affected apps in `apps/`.
use-case.goal: Keep reusable APIs stable and prevent accidental coupling to app-private internals.

use-case.action: Changes an app route, content flow, or layout only after reading the graph, workspace rules, and local module contracts.
use-case.goal: Maintain thin routes, explicit ownership boundaries, and content-driven behavior.

use-case.action: Introduces a new module or substantially refactors a high-risk file with explicit semantic scaffolding.
use-case.goal: Leave stable anchors and local contracts for future bottom-up retrieval and safe patching.

use-case.action: Reviews a repository change by comparing code, AGENTS guidance, and Compass XML documents.
use-case.goal: Detect drift between implementation, architecture, and verification expectations.

use-case.action: Uses workspace-scoped checks, structured logs, and task-specific markdown instructions to verify behavior.
use-case.goal: Assess runtime trajectories without depending only on narrow assertion coverage.

use-case.action: Handles legacy guidance in `.agents/` only after checking active `AGENTS.md` files and root Compass documents.
use-case.goal: Use historical context without allowing outdated guidance to override active rules.

changelog-os-requirements.requirement: The changelog pipeline lives in `@warpgogol/werkstatt-site/changelog` at `packages/os/site-kernel-changelog/src/changelog/` and is wired into each app via `tools/modules/changelog.module.ts`. Invoked per-app via `pnpm changelog:generate`.
All AI calls must be rate-limited (p-limit 5) and results cached in SQLite WAL mode with a composite key: TreeHash + files.sort() + diffSummary + promptHash + modelVersion.
All commit text fields must be sanitized with `sanitizeForPrompt()` before being sent to any LLM.
Breaking changes with AI confidence below `breakingChangeConfidenceThreshold` (default 0.85) must not trigger an automatic SemVer bump; they generate a warning and set `requiresReview: true`.
Major version increments are permanently forbidden. The version bumper must throw on any attempt.
Versioned changelog files must include the version in their filename: `changelog-YYYY-MM-DD-vX.Y.Z.md`.
CHANGELOG.md index must be rebuilt entirely (not appended) and dynamic markers must be restored automatically if absent.
All file writes must be atomic: write to a `.tmp` file, then `fs.rename`.

repository-requirements.requirement: `docs/requirements.xml`, `docs/technology.xml`, `docs/development-plan.xml`, `docs/knowledge-graph.xml`, `docs/verification-plan.xml`, `docs/source-markup.xml`, and `docs/styling.xml` are the mandatory repository-level semantic context for AI-driven work.
Any task that changes business intent, architecture, shared package APIs, workspace topology, or verification policy must update the affected Compass documents in the same change set.
Root and nested `AGENTS.md` files remain the active instruction hierarchy; they must direct agents to the Compass documents first when repository-wide context matters.
Legacy `.agents/**` material is reference-only and may add rationale, but it must not override active `AGENTS.md` or Compass contracts.

New source files under `apps/` and `packages/` should include Compass semantic scaffolding when the file is non-trivial: `MODULE_CONTRACT`, `MODULE_MAP`, `CHANGE_SUMMARY`, and paired semantic anchors for major blocks.

Existing files are adopted incrementally. Backfill Compass scaffolding when creating new files, when substantially editing high-risk files, or when a file has become difficult to navigate without explicit anchors.
Do not bulk-edit untouched files only to add markup if that churn is not required by the current task.
Repository documentation remains in English, including all Compass artifacts, contracts, verification notes, and migration guidance.

Shared package entrypoints, authored local TypeScript specifiers, and generator-owned app templates must remain synchronized with the active universal import/export contract described in `AGENTS.md`, `packages/AGENTS.md`, `docs/authoring/site-composition.md`, and `docs/technology.xml`.
Do not treat `spec/` or `todo/` as primary implementation authority when the same rule already exists in `AGENTS.md` or `docs/*.xml`.
Shared icon assets and generated icon components must be owned by `packages/ui`; apps consume them through `@warpgogol/ui` imports instead of restoring app-local icon trees.
Workspace-scoped site OS commands that operate on shared packages or repository-wide assets must be registered in the repository root `tools/kernel.config.ts`.

Published videos and content image tokens in `apps/*` must carry RFC-0220 material credits via `*.credits.yaml` sidecars. The credits record is the canonical source for inline disclosure, generated credits pages, and deploy-time validation.

Internal site circulation uses the RFC-0221 handoff model: thin authored-site bundles are validated and migrated forward against the recipient ecosystem by `@warpgogol/werkstatt/handoff`; `client.export` remains the external full-fork deliverable.

Deployable backend runtime compositions live in `services/*`. Services are composition-only workspaces for runtime entrypoints, deployment config, environment/store/queue selection, and health checks; reusable schemas, adapters, validators, reports, browser capture, and shared logic belong in `packages/*`.

Hierarchical demand records (RFC-0244) must use canonical folder depth (1/2/3 segments). Base city-level demand records (depth-4 children, e.g., `{industry}/{city}.md`) must set `name` to a service/demand concept, not the city name, to avoid depth-5 title tautology: `{demand.name} für {industry.name} in {city.name}` must not repeat the city.

Authored offer pillars (RFC-0243) replace PSEO-generated depth-0 listing pages. Listing pages are authored content (pageId: services) with explicit audience cards linking to authored offer detail pages. Navigation and footer links target the semantic pageId directly. Moved offer pages receive 301 redirects from their legacy URLs. The offer Blueprint no longer emits a depth-0 pillar route.

The Agent Control Plane projection (RFC-0245/RFC-0246) lives at `docs/ecosystem.generated.yaml`, is generated from live workspace state by `ecosystem.manifest.generate`, uses schema v2 deterministic metadata (`meta.generatedAt: null`, `meta.contentHash`, source hashes), derives workspace packages from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and is drift-guarded by `ecosystem.manifest.validate` plus `workspace.surface.validate` in the package validation pipeline. Agents may use it for planning context, but it is not normative.

Workspace-scoped package validation entrypoints `packages.check` and `packages-check.run` must execute targetlessly from the repository root and remain aliases over the same `PACKAGES_CHECK_PIPELINE` step list unless a later accepted RFC explicitly separates them.

Agent-facing advisory findings in standard checks must travel as canonical `Diagnostic[]` records, not only as `KernelCommandResult.summary` prose. `warning.diagnostics.lint` guards summary-only warning markers, and `maintenance.debt.report` aggregates warning/info diagnostics from app author advisory checks for return-for-rework planning.

The autonomous package quality gate (RFC-0249) is represented by `ci.local.validate` and `test.signal.validate`: CI and local agents must use the same command set for package lint, package checks, app author checks, RFC validation, tests, and test-signal classification; the Agent Control Plane records each workspace package's test signal.

Test signal maturity and maintenance debt baselines (RFC-0251) are explicit, owned, and diffable: package test skips require `gogol.testSignal` owner/rationale/review metadata, no-op test scripts are forbidden by policy validation, and `docs/maintenance-debt.baseline.generated.yaml` separates accepted advisory backlog from new debt.

Advisory maintenance debt queues (RFC-0256) convert accepted warning debt into bounded, ownerful, reviewable work plans under `docs/maintenance-debt/queues/*.yaml`; `maintenance.debt.queue.report` emits the next batch, `maintenance.debt.queue.validate` guards schema/staleness/unqueued accepted warnings, and `maintenance.debt.queue.generate` owns `docs/maintenance-debt.queues.generated.yaml`.

Runtime warnings for shared section fallback assets and semantic page targets must have canonical static diagnostic coverage. `section.defaults.validate`, `semantic.targets.validate`, and `runtime.warnings.lint` keep app-specific shared UI defaults and missing route/pageId warnings visible before Astro render logs (RFC-0250).

Long-running Site OS command and pipeline execution must expose timing and timeout telemetry. Kernel command results include command-level timing, pipeline results include total duration and slowest-step summaries, and `pipeline.timeout.validate` guards incoherent timeout metadata for standard pipeline descriptors (RFC-0255).

PSEO-capable apps must declare `surface.modules` in `src/content/system.md`. Each module owns its Blueprints exactly once, declares its own entitlement, `masterLocale`, `publishedLocales`, offline generation policy, approval policy, and localization references; `surface.context.validate` guards this context before surface generation and enrichment.

Every Sternsystem maintains an append-only Bordbuch at `systems//bordbuch/events.ndjson`. Bordbuch events are hash-chained, secret/PII-guarded, corrected through errata rather than history rewrites, and record both lifecycle events (mission open/close/abort, deployment, release) and runtime operational events (PSEO breaker trips, autonomy demotions, IndexNow submissions). Projections are generated by `bordbuch.generate` into `systems//public/.well-known/bordbuch.*` (JSON, HTML, YAML) and consumed by PSEO and fleet control loops. Enforced by `bordbuch.validate` and `bordbuch.generate`.

PSEO indexability must be gated by deterministic evidence and duplicate checks, not by structural substance alone. Blueprints may declare per-depth evidence policies; `surface.evidence.validate`, `surface.duplicate.validate`, `surface.validate`, `pseo.validate`, and `demand.modifier.lint` guard required narratives, record evidence, freshness validity, duplicate clusters, phantom levels, lazy pages, and path-safe demand slugs.

PSEO translations must follow an explicit derived-artifact lifecycle. Approved master-locale enriched artifacts are separately stamped `readyForTranslation` with a normalized `contentHash`; derived target artifacts carry `derivedFrom`, `sourceHash`, translator-note id, glossary id, and target QA state; unapproved or target-gate-failing translations must not render as indexable content.

Every PSEO module target language must have approved, current, non-public translator notes and machine-readable glossaries before translation generation can run. `surface.translation.notes.validate` and `surface.translation.glossary.validate` guard approval, source/target language metadata, required sections, moduleContextHash freshness, and term policy shape.

Search demand must be a first-class, versioned surface record source. `DemandSignal` records live under `src/content/surface/demand-signals/{lang}`, are imported only through offline aggregate exports, carry provenance and freshness, avoid PII/per-user analytics, and can gate Blueprint depths through `policy.demandPerDepth`; `demand.signal.validate`, `demand.map.report`, and `pseo.proof.validate` guard the demand-map proof surface.

Deep evidence-driven Programmatic Surface pages may be bounded by consented Werk records instead of cartesian tuples. `WerkRecord` records live under `src/content/surface/werke/{lang}`, require anchored provenance and publish/client consent, join to axis tuples through `surface.evidence.join`, and can gate Blueprint depths through `evidencePerDepth.minWerkEvidence` plus `existenceSource: works`.

PSEO approvals must carry typed authority. Autonomy scopes are declared per module, field-class, and locale with explicit level and ceiling; `autonomy.level.validate`, `autonomy.level.report`, `autonomy.promote`, and `autonomy.demote` guard calibration-backed promotion, instant demotion, typed approvers, and claims/product ceilings.

AI review is an auditable generation-lane artifact, never a deterministic build dependency. Review verdicts carry pinned reviewer identity, confidence, checks, and grounding violations; `surface.review.validate` enforces reviewer/generator separation, low-confidence escalation, and no approval with grounding violations.

Human involvement is a typed escalation budget. Escalations are routed through `src/surface/escalations.ndjson`, report human-minutes per 1000 pages, require feedback on resolution, and block when budget is exhausted instead of auto-approving under pressure.

PSEO visibility must close the measured feedback loop before autonomous expansion. Aggregate, PII-free visibility snapshots are imported offline, reconciled to generated clusters, and converted into governed cluster actions (`expand`, `hold`, `prune`, `enrich`, `escalate`) by `visibility.import`, `visibility.reconcile`, and `visibility.action.plan`; enrichment requires positive demand and outcomes feed proof/Bordbuch control surfaces.

Autonomous PSEO expansion must be reversible and breaker-guarded. `surface.generate` records content-addressed surface states with `lastKnownGood` pointers; `surface.breaker.evaluate` freezes/demotes/escalates on tripwires; rollback commands restore prior good state through pointer/noindex/redirect policy and must never delete published URLs.

Ratgeber claim records are structured, source-bound, and expiry-tracked. A dedicated content collection `surface/claims/{lang}/*.md` holds claim records with claimId, articleId, claimText, claimType, sourceRefs, calculationInputs, limitations, verifiedAt, expiresAt, and reviewStatus. `ratgeber.claim.validate` enforces schema, uniqueness, article resolution, source binding, calculation inputs, URL validity, expiry warnings, disputed status, and PBP value drift (RG-CLAIM-01..09). `ratgeber.provenance.validate` resolves claimIds against this collection (RG-PROV-03, RG-PROV-06).

Fleet-level PSEO operation must be coordinated by a stateless Leitstand over per-site primitives. `fleet.status.collect` reads per-system Bordbuch projections, autonomy, visibility, breaker, and escalation status; `fleet.schedule.plan` emits a fair, budget-clipped work queue that never clips safety jobs; `fleet.killswitch` can freeze autonomous action across the fleet without approving content or replacing site state.

Pipeline command results are cached by declared `reads` hash + module hash (RFC-0390). Every registered kernel command MUST declare `reads: string[]` (non-empty picomatch globs) or `cacheable: false`. The `command.reads.validate` command enforces this contract in `PACKAGES_CHECK_PIPELINE`. The cache reuses the existing `CacheLayer` (RFC-0382) with a `command_results` namespace; only `ok: true` results are cached. `--force` bypasses cache reads; `dryRun` bypasses entirely. All hashing uses `@warpgogol/werkstatt/fingerprint` (DNA-53).

Sites may declare `businessModel: b2b-only` in `src/content/system.md` to enforce B2B-only content constraints. When declared, `b2b.model.validate` (in `sites-check-author` pipeline) checks that no B2C consumer-protection page entries (e.g., `widerruf`, `musterWiderruf`), route slugs, navigation labels, or statutory references (§ 312g/312j BGB, Verbraucher-Widerrufsrecht) remain in content. Sites may also declare `retiredRoutes` — an array of `{ slug, status: 410 }` entries that the codegen emits as 410 Gone tombstones in `_redirects` (RFC-0487).

Ratgeber depth-1 article pages emit Article JSON-LD with structured Person author (from `authorRecord`), `description`, `mainEntityOfPage` as canonical URL string, and `dateModified` derived from `reviewedAt` or latest `changelog[].date`. FAQPage JSON-LD is prohibited on ratgeber depth-1 pages — FAQ content is rendered as visible HTML blocks only. The C-contract (`jsonld-types.yaml`) declares `FAQPage` in ratgeber depth-1 `prohibitedTypes` and `description`/`mainEntityOfPage` in Article `optional` fields. `seo.structured-data.validate` enforces SD-RAT-01..04 and `surface.contract.validate` checks the C-contract compliance.

required-elements.element: stable semantic anchors for major blocks
semantic anchors for major logical sections

source-file-contract-requirements.authority: The canonical, machine-readable definition of these modes and elements lives in `docs/source-markup.xml`.

agent-runtime-certification-program.requirement: The accepted target is one stack profile resolving an immutable graph of versioned, independently lifecycle-managed components; the one-plugin runtime is a pre-cutover implementation fact only.
The Law Kernel owns authority, canonical identity and diagnostics, grants and effects, lifecycle admission, isolation admission, certification, and promotion policy.
The transition executes packets 000 through 240 sequentially on one fixed branch with parallelism one, exact predecessor completion boundaries, and independently verified Steward/Executor roles.
A governing RFC/spec status alone never authorizes implementation; a sealed packet, exact hashes, clean trees, and the exclusive RFC-0856 lease are mandatory.
Intermediate build or deployment failure is permitted. Compatibility authority, validation downgrade, local fallback, scope widening, and parallel implementation are forbidden.
Agent-written and third-party executable artifacts remain disabled until a real admitted sandbox and the governed evolution controller are complete.

RFC-0852 (packet 030): `packages/werkstatt/src/schemas/diagnostic.ts` is the sole owner of Diagnostic strict Zod schemas and inferred types. Legacy aliases and deprecated fields are removed; `data` accepts only runtime-branded CanonicalJsonObjectV1.

RFC-0858 (packet 050): `packages/werkstatt/src/component/` owns strict versioned component manifests, capability provides/requires, grants, effects, isolation, resources, and canonical resolved-component-set identity. Unknown fields, invalid identities, duplicate provides, Law Kernel reserved grant scopes, and unknown effect/isolation/tier types fail. Canonical identity uses the existing fingerprint authority; no ad hoc hashing.

RFC-0859 (packet 060): `packages/werkstatt/src/component-runtime/` owns the structured-concurrency runtime: closed lifecycle state machine, component fibers with bounded drain and LIFO unwind, four effect handlers (revertible, transactional, compensatable, irreversible-emission), and activation transaction. No force unload, best-effort teardown, or swallowed disposer errors. Failed rollback quarantines.

RFC-0860 (packet 070): `packages/werkstatt/src/component-runtime/resolver.ts` owns pure deterministic dependency resolution — same inputs always resolve to one canonical graph/set hash. `reconciliation.ts` computes pure desired-state diff plans and drives RFC-0859 activation transactions. No package/network discovery, fallback providers, cycle tolerance, or plugin adapters.

RFC-0861 (packet 080): `packages/werkstatt/src/component-runtime/reflection.ts` owns the read-only, policy-filtered live capability catalog — entries are canonical, exact-set-bound, caller-filtered, and omit secrets, raw grants, private state, and authority material. `conformance.ts` owns scenario/result contracts where results are always test-only with no admission/promotion decision. `testing/harness.ts` owns the test-only conformance harness with guards rejecting non-test mode, untrusted fixtures, and unpinned artifacts. No production define/install/run/activate/promote command is exported.

RFC-0862 (packet 090): `packages/werkstatt/src/isolation/` owns the provider-neutral sandbox adapter contract, deny-by-default capability bridge, attenuated grants, and adversarial conformance suite. Strict Zod schemas reject unknown fields, ambient authority, invalid grants, replay, and confused identity. Twelve required security properties must be independently proven. `node:vm`, `worker_threads`, and ordinary subprocesses fail the security-tier contract by definition. Missing property evidence returns `incomplete`, never `pass`. No concrete provider or production activation is added.

RFC-0853 (packet 100): `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/` owns strict Zod schemas, inferred types, and explicit identity builders for all CERT-001 certification objects — identifiers, release candidates, policy bundles, evidence envelopes, dossier events, gate/main/health decisions, action packs, authority artifacts, and deployment operation state/events. All schemas use `.strict()` validation. Identity builders construct fresh payloads field-by-field, snapshot through RFC-0849, and hash through the engine fingerprint owner. Evidence identity enforces redaction closure. No evaluation algorithms, state cutover, storage, commands, or adapters exist.

RFC-0850 (packet 110): `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/` owns the pure deterministic evaluation pipeline — `evidence-selection.ts` builds a single-pass bounded evidence index keyed by requirement ID; `aggregation.ts` resolves requirements at an immutable evaluation cut, preserves per-requirement status, applies precedence `fail > stale > incomplete > pass`; `action-pack.ts` creates anchored remediation tasks with topological ordering; `dossier-hash.ts` computes order-sensitive event/root hashes. Hard limits: 1,000 requirements, 10,000 evidence records, 1,000 action tasks. No I/O, clock, env, or plugin imports.

RFC-0851 (packet 120): Release manifests accept only artifact readiness states `prepared` and `ready`; legacy deployment-state labels are rejected without translation. `readReleaseManifest` and `writeReleaseYaml` use strict `releaseManifestSchema` validation via the `yaml` package; manifests with legacy states throw `LegacyReleaseError`. `release.list` reports valid releases separately from `legacyInvalid` entries. All Leitstand commands and `release.rollback` are blocked with `CERT-TRANSITION-01` until CERT-007. No `--force`, `--skip-certification`, `--legacy`, compatibility, or transition-disable flag exists.

RFC-0848 (packet 130): Cross-module integration suite at `packages/werkstatt/src/tests/certification-foundation.integration.test.ts` proves ten CERT-INTEGRATION laws using public child APIs only — canonical JSON snapshotting of diagnostic/certification values, identity digest determinism, immutable evaluation cut, permutation invariance, dossier root sensitivity, fail > stale > incomplete > pass precedence, deployment/artifact separation, legacy state rejection, transition block fail-closed, and engine/plugin Diagnostic ownership boundary. No child logic is reimplemented; no adapters, aliases, or fallback passes are introduced.

CERT-002 (packet 140): `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/profile/` owns `CertificationProfileV1` strict Zod schemas, producer declarations, requirements, applicability, reuse/freshness, risk, remediation, and retention schemas. Canonical hash uses RFC-0849 fingerprint authority. `validateCertificationProfileV1` validates plugin/profile binding, duplicate IDs, producer registration, dimension coverage for all nine dimensions and Main gate paths, continuous-health freshness, rollback eligibility, and evaluator policy. No producer execution, deployment decisions, or I/O.

CERT-003 (packet 150): `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/authority/` owns issuer registry, attestation verification, signed decision/root verification — reject unregistered issuers, key mismatches, and forged signatures. `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/storage/` owns the content-addressed dossier repository with append-only event chain, chain-break detection, root hash recomputation, provider-neutral storage adapter interface, in-memory adapter, stored-object verification, retention GC with protected references, tombstones, and durable replica verification. No R2 adapter, producer orchestration, or deployment commands.

CERT-004 (packet 160): `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/orchestration/` owns producer dependency planning (topological sort with cycle detection), gate lock manager (per-release+gate mutual exclusion, idempotent re-acquire), producer execution with bounded parallelism, timeout, retry, cancellation, and progress events, and resume point computation from partial evidence. `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/commands/` owns read-only `getCertificationStatus` (candidate identity, latest decisions, coverage, durable replica status, next required action) and `verifyCertification` (candidate ID recompute, dossier integrity, root hash match, decision references). No producer implementations, deployment commands, or I/O imports.

CERT-005 (packet 170): `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/producers/` owns the deterministic producer framework — typed producer registry with duplicate rejection (`CERT-PRODUCER-01`), profile validation (`CERT-PRODUCER-03` missing, `CERT-PRODUCER-04` extra), applicability evaluation (always/entitlement/config/surface rules), false-pass guard (`CERT-PRODUCER-05` empty-result, `CERT-PRODUCER-06` summary-only warning, `CERT-PRODUCER-07` grace-period), diagnostic normalization with deduplication (`CERT-PRODUCER-08`), route/state/viewport matrix planning, and producer execution with evidence envelope construction (`CERT-PRODUCER-09` unregistered, `CERT-PRODUCER-10` handler crash, `CERT-PRODUCER-11` false-pass). No site-specific producer implementations, deployment commands, or I/O imports.

CERT-006 (packet 180): `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/evaluators/` owns the independent evaluator framework — evaluator registry with duplicate rejection (`CERT-EVAL-01`), risk routing (ordinary/critical/borderline with dimension-matched rules), evaluator isolation rejecting self-review (`CERT-EVAL-02`) and duplicate identities (`CERT-EVAL-03`), consensus aggregation (pass/pass → pass, fail/fail → fail, disagreement/missing → incomplete, `CERT-EVAL-05`), payload validation (`CERT-EVAL-07` bundle hash, `CERT-EVAL-08` rubric, `CERT-EVAL-09` confidence, `CERT-EVAL-10` criterion/rationale), evaluator execution (`CERT-EVAL-11` isolation, `CERT-EVAL-12` unregistered, `CERT-EVAL-13` crash/invalid), and coverage manifest building from deterministic evidence. No evaluator-led mutation, human approval, or I/O imports.

RFC-0863 (packet 190): `packages/werkstatt/src/capability-artifacts/` owns the immutable capability artifact store — content-addressed publication with size/media-type policy (`CERT-ARTIFACT-01` oversized, `CERT-ARTIFACT-02` unallowed media), immutability (`CERT-ARTIFACT-03` duplicate), hash verification (`CERT-ARTIFACT-04` missing, `CERT-ARTIFACT-05` mismatch), and provider admission store (`CERT-ARTIFACT-06` non-pass, `CERT-ARTIFACT-07` stale conformance). `packages/werkstatt/src/isolation/broker/` owns the deny-by-default capability bridge — ambient host access rejection (`CERT-BROKER-01` fs/net/process/env/credential/descriptor/ipc/host-object), duplicate capability rejection (`CERT-BROKER-02`), policy/grant enforcement, request/response size limits, concurrency limits, and redacted audit entries. `packages/werkstatt/src/isolation/providers/` owns the first concrete sandbox adapter implementing `IsolationAdapterV1` with all 12 required property evidence. No evolution controller, canary promotion, production agent capability, or provider-specific manifest field.

RFC-0864 (packet 200): `packages/werkstatt/src/evolution/` owns the governed capability evolution controller — forward-only sequence `defined → tested → shadowed → canary → promoted` with rollback and quarantine as compensating transitions. Contracts (`contracts.ts`) define immutable, content-addressed candidates with lineage, five-layer evidence bundles (definition, evaluation, observation, authority, artifact), and transition records.
